PILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle. Quezon City http: ltwww. dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 08 DEC A'ITY. CARLO P. LORETO Vice Governor Province of Leyte Tacloban City Dear Vice Governor Loreto: This has reference to your letter dated 15 September 2017 requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following issue you have raised. The said issue is quoted here in verbatim: "whether a VIZe Governor, who is a member of the Philippine Bar, may engage into the practice of legal profession, specifically: to appear as private counsel; to apply for notarial commission; and/or to teach in any level of any educational institutions, without securing an authorization from the DILG the Ombudsman or the Civil Service Commission. " To reiterate under Section 49 (a) of the Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 " (LGC), the vice governor is the presiding officer of the sangguniang panlalawigan, quoted hereunder is the said provision: "Section 49. Presiding Officer. - (a) The vice-governor shall be the presiding officer of the sangguniang panlalawigan; the city vice-mayor, of the sangguniang panlungsod; the municipal vice-mayor, of the sangguniang bayan; and the punong barangay, of the sangguniang barangay. The presiding officer shall vote only to break a tie. " It is a well-settled rule that a vice governor is a member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Logically, the provision under Section 90 of the LGC pertaining to the practice of profession of a local elective official shall apply to him. The said provision is quoted hereunder: "Section 90. Practice of Profession. -

(a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. (b) Sanggunian members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours: Provided, That sanggunian members who are also members of the Bar shall not: (I) Appear as counsel before any court in any civil case wherein a local government unit or any office, agency, or instrumentality of the government is the adverse party; (2) Appear as counsel in any criminal case wherein an officer or employee of the national or local government is accused of an offense committed in relation to his office. (3) Collect any fee for their appearance in administrative proceedings involving the local government unit of which he is an official; and (4) Use property and personnel of the government except when the sanggunian member concerned is defending the interest of the government. (c) Doctors of medicine may practice their profession even during official hours of work only on occasions of emergency: Provided, That the officials concerned do not derive monetary compensation therefrom. " (Emphasis supplied) Relevant thereto, Section 7 (b) (2) of RA 6713, otherwise known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees", provides that the public officials and employees, such as the vice governor, may practice their profession provided that that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their official functions. The relevant provision of the said law is quoted hereunder: "Section Z Prohibited Acts and Transactions. — (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto. - Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: (2) Engage in the private practice of their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law, provided, that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their official functions• or"

In DILG Legal Opinion No. 085-96 dated 29 October 1996, we stated the following rule regarding a sanggunian member's authority to practice of profession: "T'he Code allows sanggunian members to practice their profession, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools outside of session hours. There is no need for permission from other person or office (The Local Government Code of 1991. "The Key to National Development", Pimentel, p. 204). " In relation thereto, the Supreme Court (SC) in Catu vs. Rellosal reiterated the rule that the members of the sanggunian does not need to secure prior permission or authorization from any other person or office for them to practice their profession. The relevant portion of the decision is also quoted hereunder: On the other hand, members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours. In other words, they may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools outside their session hours. Unlike governors, city mayors and municipal mayors, members of the sangguniangpanlalawigan, sangguniangpanlungsod or sangguniang bayan are required to hold regular sessions only at least once a week. Since the la w itself grants them the authority topractice their professions, engage in any occupation or teach in schools outside session hours, there is no n er for riza other person or office for an V of these purposes. With these legal precepts in mind, we hope that the Department has enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours: By Authori f the Secretary: AUSTERE A.
